entities.name: Emperor Zhang of Han
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Emperor Zhang of Han was the third emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty, reigning from 75 to 88 CE. He succeeded his brother Emperor Zhao and expanded the Silk Road trade network.

Zhang's reign saw significant military campaigns against the Xiongnu confederation in northern China, which led to the establishment of the Chinese border with modern-day Mongolia.

Despite facing economic challenges due to a decline in tax revenues and a costly war effort, Zhang maintained stability throughout his rule.

The emperor's efforts to maintain control over the vast territories of the Eastern Han dynasty had significant consequences for the regional dynamics of ancient China.

As the empire expanded under his leadership, trade and cultural exchange flourished along the Silk Road, shaping the course of Chinese history.

Zhang's legacy also includes the construction of the Great Wall, a testament to the engineering prowess and military might of the Eastern Han dynasty.

The Silk Road's prosperity during Zhang's reign is remembered as one of the most significant achievements of his rule.
